sample_unit: prospectively collected low-quality endoscopic images (plus public KVASIR-SEG and GIANA images)
models_evaluated: commonly-used DNN architectures for polyp segmentation/detection

links.outcome: Performance drop under clinically calibrated image degradations and mitigation by architecture and pretraining
links.effect: Performance declined 11.6% (±1.5) versus reference under degradations; advanced architectures and self-supervised in-domain pre-training reduced the drop to 7.7% (±2.03).
links.quote: The results reveal a considerable decline in performance of 11.6% (±1.5) as compared to the reference, within the clinically calibrated boundaries of image degradations.

links.outcome: Performance loss from domain gap between development data and real-world endoscopic images
links.effect: Domain gap between high-quality development images and clinical input produced an 11.6% (±1.5) performance decline under calibrated degradations.
links.quote: This so-called domain gap between the data used for developing the system and the data it encounters after deployment, and the impact it has on the performance of deep neural networks (DNNs) supportive endoscopic CAD systems remains largely unexplored.

unlisted_practices: Self-supervised in-domain pre-training and data augmentation to improve robustness of imaging DNNs

screen.reason: The study conducts a safety and robustness stress-test on endoscopic CADe/CADx models using clinically calibrated image degradations and evaluates mitigation strategies against domain gaps.

primary.practice: stress testing with synthetic clinically calibrated image degradations and robustness strategies
